title: From equitable to promissory estoppel
summary: The chapter distinguishes reliance on a representation of fact from reliance on promised future conduct.
notes: Ricketts is part of the transition: a gift promise induced departure from employment, and the court prevented reliance on lack of consideration. The notes trace historical categories in which courts protected reliance, including family land improvements, gratuitous bailments, and charity. The modern section 90 formulation makes the forward-looking promise explicit; the historical labels alone do not settle its elements.
